name: What should I compare when choosing between attached and detached ADU construction?

mainEntity.name: Which factors matter most when deciding whether an attached ADU or detached ADU is the better investment for my property?
mainEntity.text: Which factors matter most when deciding whether an attached ADU or detached ADU is the better investment for my property?

acceptedAnswer.text: Choosing between attached and detached ADU construction comes down to how the property is used, not just which option sounds better. Attached ADUs are often a better fit for smaller or tighter lots because they use existing structure and may avoid some site constraints. They can also be more efficient if the homeowner wants to expand the main house while adding separate living space. Detached ADUs, on the other hand, usually provide stronger privacy, better rental appeal, and more separation from the main residence. The tradeoff is that they often require more yard space and can cost more because they need their own full structure. Homeowners should compare construction cost, permit complexity, utility upgrades, outdoor space loss, and resale appeal. The best choice is usually the one that matches the property’s physical constraints and the owner’s long-term use case. A quick feasibility study can prevent choosing the wrong ADU type based on cost alone.
acceptedAnswer.description: The key factors are cost, privacy, lot size, setbacks, utility complexity, and how the unit will be used. Attached ADUs are often better for constrained lots and lower site disruption, while detached ADUs usually offer more independence and stronger separation from the main home.
